title: Asymmetric feedback digest and priorities
content:
Purpose: quick, evidence-backed notes to bring to my upcoming check-in. A compact digest so manager conversation stays focused on impact and decisions, not background. Use this as the single source for the next 3 checkpoints (monthly).

Top-line ask (1 sentence): Recommend a path to expand into program-level enablement (lead of onboarding ops) — want to validate scope and a small stretch IC step with measurable impact over next 6 months.

Signals and concrete examples (what I will show / say):
- Onboarding time reduction: partnered with Eng onboarding team to remove 2 redundant steps in access flow (ticket: JIRA-OPS-789). Measured: new hires complete initial access in median 18h -> 9h over pilot (n=12).
- Cost/efficiency: designed new SLAs for contractor intake that cut approvals backlog by 40% (tracked in spreadsheet /confluence id above). Saved ~60 engineer-hours in Q4 by eliminating duplicate approvals.
- Reliability/ops: created a lightweight runbook for new-hire hardware allocation that reduced mis-ship incidents from 5 -> 1 in last quarter (incident refs in slack thread).
- Influence: led two cross-functional retros with PM/Eng/IT; outcomes included a shared metric we now track weekly (new-hire time-to-first-prod).

Feedback samples (asymmetric notes I’ve received — paraphrased):
- "Very pragmatic: digs to the issue and ships a simple fix." (Eng manager)
- "Could be more proactive about creating clear success criteria for projects." (Peer)
- "Great stakeholder wrangling but sometimes scope creeps without explicit tradeoffs." (Product partner)
- "High ownership — could benefit from clearer delegation when leading initiatives." (Manager)

Interpretation / self-reflection (what this means for my next role):
- Strengths: execution bias, process-slimming, cross-team influence. These map well to a program lead role.
- Gaps to close: defining measurable success criteria up-front; clearer delegation and org-level communication; framing tradeoffs for leadership.

Concrete 3-month experiments (metrics & how I’ll measure):
1) Success criteria template: for every new intake project, add a 1-line success metric in PRD or ticket. Measurement: 100% of tickets for next 8 projects contain a metric; review during retro.
2) Delegation habit: for initiatives >2 stakeholders, explicitly assign an owner and 1 deputy within first 2 weeks. Measurement: ownership fields filled in tickets; reduction in rework loops by 20%.
3) Tradeoff one-pager: for two live projects, produce a one-pager that lists options, costs (hours), and expected outcomes; present in manager check-in. Measurement: manager feedback and whether one-pager used for prioritization.

Manager conversation prompts (what I’ll ask):
- Based on the pilot onboarding metrics, do you see program-level opportunity or should I double-down on execution within operational remit?
- Which of these experiments would you sponsor or unblock? (ask for specific resource/time commitments)
- How will success for a stretch step be evaluated from your perspective in 3 and 6 months? (ask for 2–3 clear signals)
- Are there stakeholders you think I should bring in earlier to accelerate cross-org adoption?

Risks / escalation plan (if things go sideways):
- If I can’t secure stakeholder time: shrink scope to 1 team pilot and label as "proof-of-value."
- If metrics don’t move: capture lessons and propose a second hypothesis rather than continue unsuccessful tactics.

Draft ask wording (for the meeting):
"I’d like to propose a small stretch into program-level onboarding enablement: run a 3-team pilot to formalize success criteria and handoffs, with defined metrics (time-to-first-prod and approval backlog). If pilot reaches our targets, I propose a follow-up to scope a recurring role/responsibility. I’m asking for your help to unblock two stakeholder commitments and to make the pilot a priority for Q2"

Quick evidence appendix (links & where to find things):
- Pilot access flow spreadsheet: confluence://page/CONFLUENCE-3332 (pilot dataset + before/after)
- Ticket backlog reduction: JIRA-OPS-912 (ticket list and SLA changes)
- Incident log references: slack:#onboarding-incidents (thread pinned Feb 2026)
- Output templates: google doc "onboarding-criteria-template-v1" in my drive (private)

Open questions to resolve before meeting (research actions):
- Is there a current hiring freeze signal I should account for? (ask Finance/HR)
- What is the threshold our manager wants for converting a pilot into a recurring role? (ask manager)
- Who is the single exec advocate to elevate this to if we need headcount? (identify with manager)

Next steps (timeline):
- By Mar 5: finalize success-criteria template and apply to 2 live intake tickets.
- By Mar 12: secure stakeholder commitments from Eng onboarding and IT procurement for pilot scope.
- Mar 17 check-in: bring one-pager and initial metric snapshots to manager meeting.

Notes to self / conversational tone reminders:
- Start the meeting with the single-sentence ask. Avoid walking through every detail unless asked.
- Bring the numbers first (time, reduction %, hours saved).
- When asked about tradeoffs, always offer 2 options (fast/simple vs. broader/longer).
- Invite the manager to shape evaluation criteria — I want them invested in the success signals.

Quick personal micro-goals for growth (behavioral):
- Before each weekly sync: write 3 clear success metrics for active projects.
- After delegating: note who I delegated to and follow-up cadence in a single tracker.
- Monthly: solicit one upward feedback item about clarity of delegation.

This is a living note — update after each manager check-in. Keep the evidence links current and keep the appendix small (max 4 docs).

Unresolved thoughts:
- Would a short internal workshop accelerate adoption? too heavy vs. one-pager? Experiment: run a 30 min "success criteria" lab with 3 teams and measure adoption.
- If the manager wants faster wins, have a fallback pilot that only targets the approvals backlog (smaller stakeholder set).

End.
